To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high-resolution imaging demonstrates characteristic epithelial and stromal changes in Schnyder cornea.
multimodal imaging of SCD shows diffuse hyperreflectivity in the corneal stroma and in the epithelius, hyporeflectivity of stromal stria and epithelial hyperreflexivity.
multimodal imaging demonstrates characteristic findings of Schnyder dystrophy involving both the epithelium as well as the stroma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the analysis of the optical properties of the cornea.
the development of a novel method for the analysis of the corneal crystals in the corneal dystrophies.
the study of the corneal dystrophies, a group of rare diseases that affect the cornea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCD is a corneal disease that affects the epithelium as well as the stroma.

Schnyder Cornea Dystrophy (SCD) is a corneal dystrophic disease that is characterized by the presence of vacuoles in the corneal stroma, and that is caused by a defect in the cholesterol 7α-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) gene, which leads to the accumulation of cholesterol esters and cholesteryl esters in the cornea.
the epithelial changes in Schnyder cornea dystrophy are a consequence of the epithelial basement membrane degeneration and that the stromal changes are a consequence of abnormal lipid accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of multimodal imaging techniques provides an important tool for the diagnosis of Schnyder crystalline dystrophy.
the multimodal imaging techniques are able to provide an accurate and reliable diagnosis of SCD even when no corneal crystals are visible at slit-lamp exam.
the combination of SD-OCT, IVCM, and FF-OCT provides an accurate description of SCD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multimodal imaging features of SCD are characteristic, allowing for diagnosis confirmation, even in eyes with only subtle corneal opacities at slit lamp.
high-resolution imaging is useful for the diagnosis of SCD, and it may be used to differentiate it from other types of corneal dystrophies with similar clinical appearance.
multimodal in vivo imaging is a valuable tool for diagnosis of SCD.
